messages:
Marta: Heads-up — found a UX gap with SLO preview cards during rollout. If an aggressive quieting policy kicks in we lose escalation mapping and it becomes hard to tell if alerts are intentionally suppressed or missing.
Kevin: ugh yep saw that in the canary yesterday. the card just shows green and no escalation path, confusing. :confused:
Jamie: can you sketch what you'd want on the card? a tiny timeline + who would be paged?
Marta: exactly. idea: add a compact 'fidelity band' and 'escalation fingerprint' on the card. fidelity band = confidence that current threshold reflects real risk (low/med/high). escalation fingerprint = the effective routing chain if an alert fires.
Sam: +1. also need a 'snapback' indicator — when quieting is lifted and alerts may surge, preview should say "expected surge risk". customers kept asking why nothing fired then all at once.
Kevin: this seems like two parts: console UI and preview API. For the API we could add fields like: 
```json
{
  "preview": {
    "fidelity": "low",
    "escalation": ["team-a", "oncall-rotation-2"],
    "snapback_risk": "medium"
  }
}
```
Marta: that payload looks good. also show sample noisy signals that would have been suppressed (one-liners, links). quick way to inspect: show 3 example traces.
Jamie: UI nit: keep the card compact. small icons + hover tooltip for details (click to expand). default collapsed state for tenants.
Sam: telemetry ask: we should emit preview-metric with fields {fidelity_score, suppression_ratio, expected_fanout}. this lets SRE ops detect bad quieting heuristics.
Marta: agreed. @ops-bot can we add a 'preview-run' event to the existing SLO-preview telemetry stream?
ops-bot: noted. I created ticket INF-8732 and scheduled a job to log a sample preview event for the next canary.
Kevin: one more API thing — we need versioning. if we add fidelity fields later we must not break older clients. propose v2 header or a namespaced preview.v2.
Jamie: +1 on namespaced field. also UX rollout: dark launch the fidelity badge behind a flag for 2 weeks. gather qualitative feedback from SEs.
Marta: sounds good. I'll prototype the card with mock data and paste a screenshot here tomorrow. for implementation: frontend -> preview API enrichment -> telemetry hook.
Sam: linking to runbook: https://confluence/internal/slo-rollout-best-practices (adds guidance on snapback ops).
Kevin: if anyone wants to push a minimal API design I can jump on the backend changes next sprint.
Marta: thanks all — will follow up with mock and a short acceptance checklist. :thumbsup:
